narrative.whats_happened:
Sightline Retail's first technical validation call covered Segment Studio end to end. Paul Renner, Data Engineer, walked through the current manual segment-request process and pushed hard on whether Apex would repeat a prior self-serve tool's failure mode, requiring constant backend babysitting. Aditi Sharma gave concrete architectural differences and was upfront that some setup work is real, not zero-maintenance.

Amara Diallo, Director of Growth Analytics, confirmed she owns budget for this category and doesn't expect a difficult internal sell. Both destinations Sightline needs, Klaviyo and Meta/Google paid social, are already supported.

Nothing is currently blocking. A priced proposal is due by end of week, with a follow-up already on the calendar.

not_blocking: Segment Studio requires real one-time setup work and isn't zero-maintenance long-term (e.g. renamed columns need updates) — Paul and Amara explicitly accepted this as a reasonable tradeoff.
Complex segment logic (rolling-window comparisons) sometimes needs a one-time custom field from someone technical — accepted as an occasional, not constant, need.

ae_actions: Send a priced proposal to Amara and Paul by end of week.
Confirm the Tuesday follow-up call and include the proposal beforehand.
narrative.sc_loop_close: Nothing technical is blocking this deal. Every concern Paul raised — schema evolution, sync-failure visibility, complex segment logic, service-account permissions — got a direct, honest answer, including the parts that aren't zero-maintenance. Paul and Amara both explicitly said the honest framing landed better than a vendor promising no tradeoffs.
sc_actions: Send Paul the specific service-account permission list (4-5 grants).

stage_exit_criteria.criterion: All technical objections resolved or accepted
Next step scheduled with owner and date
Success criteria captured in customer's words

stakeholders.name: Amara Diallo
stakeholders.title: Director, Growth Analytics
stakeholders.evidence: I do have budget allocated for something in this category for this fiscal year... if the number's in a reasonable range I don't anticipate this being a hard internal sell.

stakeholders.name: Paul Renner
stakeholders.title: Data Engineer
stakeholders.evidence: Can I push on one more piece of it though, sorry — what about when segments get genuinely complicated...

objections.text: Will Segment Studio become another full-time babysitting job like a prior self-serve tool
objections.resolution_note: Live schema reads and monitored/alerted syncs address the core fear, but Aditi explicitly concedes it's not zero-maintenance (a renamed column needs a segment update) — a real conceded limitation Amara and Paul accepted, not a concern made untrue.

objections.text: Does the visual builder handle genuinely complex segment logic (joins, rolling-window comparisons)
objections.resolution_note: Joins across modeled entities are handled natively; rolling-window comparisons sometimes need a one-time custom field from someone technical. Paul accepted this as an occasional need, not a recurring bottleneck.

objections.text: What permissions would the Apex service account need, given restricted PII tables
objections.resolution_note: Scoped to specific schemas/views, 4-5 grants, not account-admin. Paul asked for the actual permission list to bring to IT rather than raising further concern.

integration_patterns.description: Warehouse-native activation — queries run directly against Sightline's Snowflake instance, no data copied into an Apex-controlled store
Destination sync to existing marketing stack
integration_patterns.caveats: Both already-supported destination types; not new integration work.

success_criteria.customer_words: a simple one, maybe same day, few hours... if it's a more complex segment... it can be two, three days
success_criteria.interpreted: Segment requests currently take same-day to several days depending on complexity, with additional cycles when the first draft doesn't match intent.

success_criteria.customer_words: our best performing campaigns last year were the more targeted ones by like a wide margin
success_criteria.interpreted: Targeted campaigns already outperform batch-and-blast internally, giving a data-backed case for more personalization, not just a stated preference.

competitive.context_verbatim: we tried a tool a couple years back... it was constantly out of sync with the warehouse and marketing was targeting people based on data that was like a week stale, and it caused a whole thing with a customer getting an email about a product they'd already returned.
competitive.rationale: Historical, closed evaluation predating this deal; raised as context for skepticism about data freshness, not a live comparison.

competitive.context_verbatim: we tried a 'self-serve' tool a few years back, different vendor... it required so much configuration and troubleshooting on the backend that Paul ended up basically babysitting it full time anyway
competitive.rationale: Historical, closed evaluation; directly informs obj_01 and obj_02 rather than being a live competitive comparison.

next_step.described: Sofia sends a priced proposal by end of week; Sofia, Amara, Paul, and Aditi reconvene the following Tuesday to review it.
